column3: “Acquired” is rendered “provided,” and “who ran before him” as “as runners before him.”
NASB uses habitual forms (“used to rise early,” “would call”); “a case at law” is rendered “a suit.”
“Your matter” is rendered “your claims,” and “one who hears” as “no man listens to you.”
“Who will make me a judge?” is rendered as a wish (“Oh that one would appoint me judge”).
“Bow down” is rendered “prostrate himself.”
Close to the Hebrew; “stole the heart” is rendered “stole away the hearts.”
NASB follows the Hebrew “forty years.” The number is often questioned, since some ancient versions read “four.”
NASB follows the Hebrew text, without the Septuagint addition “in Hebron.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Ram’s horn” is rendered “trumpet,” and “has become king” as “is king.”
“Going to their innocence” is rendered “went innocently.”
NASB supplies “for,” and “going and numerous” is rendered “increased continually.”
“The heart of the man of Israel is after Absalom” is rendered “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”
“There will not be an escape for us” is rendered “otherwise none of us shall escape,” and “thrust calamity on us” as “bring down calamity on us.”
NASB supplies “are ready to do.”
“At his feet” is rendered “with him,” and “ten women concubines” as “ten concubines.”
“At his feet” is rendered “with him,” and “the house of the distance” as “the last house.”
“At his foot” is rendered “with him.”
NASB supplies “return” before “to your own place.”
“Yesterday your coming” is rendered “You came only yesterday,” and “covenant loyalty and truth” as “mercy and truth.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Come and pass on” is rendered “Go and pass over.”
“All the land” is rendered “all the country,” and “wadi” as “brook.”
NASB supplies “came,” and “went up” (of Abiathar) is rendered “came up”; the Hebrew may mean he offered sacrifices.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew הֲרוֹאֶה is difficult (“Are you a seer?” or “Look!”); NASB renders “Are you not a seer?”
“I will delay” is rendered “I am going to wait,” and “desert plains” (Hebrew written text) as “fords” (the reading tradition).
Close to the Hebrew.
“The ascent of the olive trees” is rendered “the ascent of the Mount of Olives.”
